A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAMTok and contain complete, readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated content can be matched reliably; appendix and reference pages 13–27 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAMTok benchmark results, supervised-versus-RL comparisons, and quantization ablations in Section 3 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, RL comparisons, ablations, and qualitative examples reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same SAM-based encoder/decoder, two-step residual quantization, mask-token interface, training objectives, and GRPO mask reward. No algorithmic or architectural component changes.

E1.justification: The training datasets and evaluated tasks remain unchanged, including GCG, GRES, referring and interactive segmentation, grounding, region captioning, and panoptic scene graph generation. Appendices C–E retain the same additional evaluations and scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. For example, Table 1 retains LISA, GLaMM, OMG-LLaVA, and Sa2VA; Table 3 retains LISA, SAM4MLLM, MLLMSeg, HiMTok, and ARGenSeg.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, model sizes, training settings, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. This includes single-frame VideoRefer-D evaluation in Table 9 and the EntitySeg reconstruction protocol in Appendix D.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains identical quantization-strategy and codebook-size/step ablations in Tables 12–13. Appendix E also preserves the RL-versus-SFT comparisons, reconstruction examples, and downstream qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and cross-split averages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–13 and qualitative findings are retained. For example, the 3B RL model has GCG validation AP50 of 41.5 in Table 1 and GRES average gIoU of 76.7 in Table 3 in both versions.

T1.justification: The encoder/decoder definitions, residual quantization, training loss, and mask reward in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-token mask representation, unified mask understanding and generation, benchmark performance, and reinforcement learning with textual rewards.

C2.justification: Interpretations of text–mask alignment, generalization, and RL effects are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning video-mask reconstruction and support for visual entities beyond masks.

D1.justification: Appendix B preserves the initialization, codebooks, token formats, optimizer settings, learning rates, batch sizes, and hardware details. Data preprocessing, the project link, and stated code/model availability also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 retains the same research positioning and comparisons with prior approaches. All 102 references are unchanged, with no cited works added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 revises author-role markers and contact information, adds an internship acknowledgment, updates the date, and corrects 'a encoder' to 'an encoder' in Figure 2's caption. Scientific prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title-page layout and main-text pagination change. Figure 4 moves from page 6 to 7, Table 3 from page 7 to 8, and Table 8 from page 9 to 10. Figure content, table structures, and appendix layouts are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 makes small editorial and attribution updates while preserving the method, evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The grammar correction and layout reflow do not create a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
